village: Space, Foundational Advance, Software & AI, Biomanufacturing
tagline: A four-enzyme cocktail plus a hydroxyapatite-binding antimicrobial peptide coating that dismantles dental plaque biofilm before it mineralises into calculus.
summary: DCO is a three-module biological oral care system: an enzyme cocktail that degrades the organic matrix holding plaque biofilm together, a tooth-binding antimicrobial peptide that coats enamel to block re-colonisation, and a controlled-release system to coordinate them. The enzymes are two recombinantly expressed glycoside hydrolases — PmGH87 (alpha-1,3-glucanase) and CoGH66 (alpha-1,6-glucanase), which act cooperatively because CoGH66 removes alpha-1,6 branches and exposes new PmGH87 cleavage sites — plus commercially sourced DNase I and papain for extracellular DNA and protein. It addresses a real and specific burden: 96.7% of Chinese adults aged 35-44 have dental calculus, over 900 million have periodontal disease, only 20.1% of elderly people saw a dentist in the past year, and the dentist-to-population ratio is about 1:7,768. It won Best Village Project on a tight problem-to-product chain, a FoldX mutation-prioritisation pipeline whose prediction was wrong and whose failure is reported in full, and an unusually commercially literate entrepreneurship section that refuses to make anti-calculus claims it cannot support.
awards: Best Village Project winner (Space / Foundational Advance / Software & AI / Biomanufacturing)

dry.frameworks: Two computational pipelines, both modest in tooling but well-reasoned and, importantly, both reported against their experimental outcome. (1) A CoGH66 mutation prioritisation pipeline built to avoid screening hundreds of mutants in the wet lab. Starting from the substrate-bound structure PDB 8IUB (CoGH66 with isomaltotriose bound, so no re-docking was needed), they used PyMOL to extract all protein residues within 4.0 A of the substrate, giving an 18-residue binding pocket (Y166, D167, Q169, Q172, I190, Y217, L219, H250, L252, F256, I260, D293, L295, N395, K429, E430, Y431, N434) consistent with the published catalytic cleft and +2 to -4 subsites. Domain annotation came from CD-Search (Glyco_hydro_66 at residues 22-560, E-value 0) and InterPro (glycosidases at 104-440), with sequence translation via Novopro. They then layered evolutionary information: BLASTp against the NCBI non-redundant protein database, deliberately selecting homologs from different bacterial species at 30-70% identity to avoid over-representing near-identical sequences and to capture naturally tolerated substitutions, aligned with MAFFT and visualised as an ESPript conservation map. Of the 18 contact residues, seven (Y166, Q169, Q172, I190, H250, N395, K429) showed species-specific natural substitutions and were taken as plastic; the remaining eleven were conserved and deliberately left alone. Mutants were built in PyMOL, repaired and scored in FoldX for both stability change and binding change, with an operational priority threshold of binding delta-delta-G < -1 kcal/mol chosen explicitly because it exceeds typical FoldX error. (2) Antimicrobial peptide selection: after a literature review identified four hydroxyapatite-binding AMP candidates, they used AlphaFold Server to predict peptide-calcium ion coordination as a first computational filter, reasoning that hydroxyapatite presents Ca2+ as the primary interaction site, and ranked candidates by pTM and interface pTM (ipTM) scores. SHABP (21 aa, cyclic and disulfide-constrained) and G12R (18 aa, linear alpha-helical) both reached pTM around 0.4, above DNase-fused and HBAMP alternatives, and both were advanced into parallel experimental validation on the grounds of their distinct structural strategies (conformational stability versus membrane disruption).
dry.dataviz: The model page leads with a schematic workflow diagram of the whole mutation-prioritisation pipeline, so the logic from structure to alignment to energy calculation is readable before any numbers appear, and ends with a three-dimensional localisation figure placing the two prioritised positions in the pocket (protein green, mutated positions red with arrows, substrate yellow, other 4.0 A contacts cyan). The genuinely notable choice is an interactive 3D model of the CoGH66-isomaltotriose complex embedded in the wiki as a glTF file exported from PyMOL, so a reader can rotate the enzyme and inspect the contact residues rather than squint at a static render — a cheap but effective way to make a structural argument inspectable. Tables carry the natural substitutions observed per non-conserved position with counts, and the full FoldX energy results for every tested mutant rather than only the winners. Measurement figures pair the physical artefact with its quantification throughout: a 96-well plate photograph alongside the bar chart derived from it for the DNS reducing-sugar assay, the crystal violet extracts, and the acridine orange fluorescence images with the ImageJ intensity quantification in the identical group order so the reader can check the numbers against the wells. Standard curves are shown with their regression equations and R2 values (BCA at Y = 0.8964X - 0.2574, R2 = 0.9951).
dry.datascience: The most valuable dry-lab content is a documented computational failure. The pipeline predicted Y166Q as the top candidate (the only mutant meeting the -1 kcal/mol binding threshold, at -1.63 kcal/mol) with Q172P as a secondary candidate retained despite only -0.38 kcal/mol because of its predicted stabilising effect and natural occurrence in homologs. Site-directed mutagenesis (reverse PCR with back-to-back mutation-carrying primers, DpnI digestion of methylated parental template, self-ligation), colony PCR at the expected ~1726 bp, and Sanger sequencing confirmed both constructs (Y166Q TAC to CAG; Q172P CAG to CCG). The DNS activity assay then inverted the ranking: Q172P gave the highest apparent activity at net OD 1.881, wild type 0.996, and Y166Q only 0.629 — the computational winner was worse than wild type. The team's response is the right one: they revised the ranking in the text, named Q172P the leading experimental candidate, reclassified Y166Q as a mechanistic probe rather than quietly dropping it, and had already flagged in advance that Q172P introduces a proline and may alter main-chain conformation so its FoldX estimate should be read with caution. They also controlled the comparison properly rather than letting protein load explain the result: BCA quantification gave WT 12.1, Y166Q 10.9 and Q172P 9.1 microgram/mL, crude lysates were normalised to equal total protein before the DNS assay, and the wiki explicitly notes that Q172P's lower total protein means its activity signal cannot be attributed to a higher load. The measurement work on the artificial dental calculus model is similarly self-critical. Gravimetric analysis of six treatment conditions (negative control, four single-component omissions, complete cocktail) found no significant weight-loss differences, and the team attributed this to balance sensitivity and to non-uniform mineralisation producing variability that masked the effect, then moved to more sensitive assays rather than reporting a null as a result. Crystal violet quantification at OD gave the complete cocktail a significant reduction against the negative control (p < 0.05), with the papain-omission comparison reported honestly as a trend toward significance at p = 0.08 and interpreted as papain playing a supporting rather than dominant role under single-treatment conditions. Acridine orange fluorescence with ImageJ quantification showed significance against the negative control and against the DNase-I-omission group, supporting the mechanistic model that eDNA cleavage lets the other enzymes penetrate, while the overall small between-group differences led them to conclude that the primary mode of action is structural matrix dismantling rather than direct bactericidal potency. Limitations are stated plainly, including that the B. subtilis surrogate model does not replicate the Streptococcus mutans-specific EPS composition the glucanases actually target. The AlphaFold peptide screen also carries its own caveat: the team notes that peptide-Ca2+ coordination cannot fully replicate crystal-surface binding, that pTM around 0.4 indicates only moderate confidence, and that the scores were used for relative ranking rather than as affinity estimates.
dry.software: No standalone released software tool; the dry lab is a documented analysis pipeline rather than a product, and the wiki itself is a React/Vite single-page application with GSAP animation. Released reusable resources instead: the full mutation-prioritisation methodology as a reproducible protocol, the interactive glTF structural model, PDF slide decks for all four education audiences (two elementary sessions dated 5-28 and 6-11, a high school deck, and an elderly-residents deck), a consolidated enzyme stabilisation and controlled-release guide offered as a generalised framework for multi-enzyme formulations across biocatalysis, food processing and environmental remediation, and a 'lessons learned for future iGEM teams' section. Constructs were expressed from codon-optimised genes in pET-32a via seamless cloning, carrying an N-terminal thioredoxin (TrxA) tag for soluble expression, a 6xHis tag for IMAC purification and an enterokinase site for optional tag removal, under T7 promoter control in E. coli Rosetta(DE3), with CoGH66 confirmed at approximately 76.54 kDa. The team also documented a safety-driven substitution they consulted the iGEM committee about: because Streptococcus mutans is not on the iGEM White List they used B. subtilis as a surrogate in the artificial calculus model, and because Aspergillus niger is not listed they used commercially available edible fungi as a material source.

good.publicEngagement: Four-tier education (primary school, high school, elderly residents, general public) with the explicit design principle that they did not just teach knowledge but recorded what changed after participants went home — brushing, flossing, denture care, diet, dental visits and attitudes toward synthetic biology. The best single tool is a tangible genetic circuit built from electronic building blocks: a touch sensor stands for the promoter, a toggle switch module for the lac operator, a button for lactose as inducer, an LED for the RBS, a small fan for the target gene and a manual power-off switch for the terminator, so children physically discover that touching the sensor alone does nothing because the operator blocks by default, and that the circuit only runs when the inducer is held. For younger children they wrote child-friendly science comics and ran plaque disclosing tablets as a reveal — children chewed the tablets, rinsed, saw red and blue patches on their own teeth, were asked to guess and ask questions first, and were then shown microscope images with the framing 'this is not dirt, this is a city'. The team records the emotional shift honestly: children moved from fearing bacteria to being curious about them and from passive listening to asking and designing. High school sessions used a full script and deck covering project background, enzyme mechanism, experimental process and application value, and specifically targeted the soft-plaque-versus-hard-calculus confusion. The nursing home session simplified everything into plain language and images and delivered concretely actionable care: a soft-bristled small-headed brush at 45 degrees to the gumline, gentle brushing with no horizontal scrubbing, bedtime brushing more important than morning, floss or interdental brushes rather than toothpicks, and denture care rules (rinse after meals, remove and soak overnight, never boiling water, never toothpaste, never sleep in them), with the explicit disclaimer that this is science communication and does not replace professional dental advice. Public outreach at Wushan Square used display boards, roll-up banners, hand fans and leaflets on plaque versus calculus and scaling misconceptions.
good.ihp: Twelve named advisors spanning clinical dentistry, periodontics, microbial control, pharmaceutics, gene circuit regulation, management and marketing, and oral care product regulatory and quality management, engaged in a staged problem-framing process. Problem framing combined a 350-respondent user questionnaire, an in-depth clinical interview with Dr. Lei Lihong (Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine) and an industry interview with Mr. Fan Wenjun (healthcare investment), triangulated against the Fourth National Oral Health Epidemiological Survey specifically to avoid bias from a single interview source. The survey quantified both misconception and the knowing-doing gap: 61% worry that scaling damages enamel, 23% believe brushing removes calculus, only 6% claim to fully understand it; and separately, 52% know calculus forms at the gingival margin and in deep interdental spaces but only 25% floss or use an irrigator daily, 48% know brushing cannot remove calculus but only 38% get scaling once or twice a year, and 84% know calculus causes periodontitis but only 25% have a six-monthly examination. The project-defining intervention came from Dr. Wang Yongwu (Hangzhou First People's Hospital), who said that using enzymes to dissolve already-mineralised calculus is 'like an egg hitting a stone' — and the team did not just accept the efficacy point but derived a safety consequence from it: because calculus and enamel and dentin are both calcium phosphate mineralised tissues, any non-selective demineralising agent would risk enamel or dentin demineralisation, sensitivity or erosion. That reframed the entire target from mineralised calculus to the organic matrix of the early pre-mineralisation biofilm, which is the intervention window the whole project now occupies. Dr. Lei and Dr. Yuan Yifang (Affiliated Stomatological Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University) corroborated it and specified what to attack: the polysaccharide-protein cross-linking and the stabilising role of eDNA that together hold the biofilm's three-dimensional structure against salivary washing. Four design constraints emerged from the interview set — efficacy validation, penetration ability, cytotoxicity safety and stability assurance — which became the selection criteria for the enzyme cocktail and delivery system. A second concrete pivot: experts pointed out that enzymatic removal does not prevent recolonisation because salivary proteins form a pellicle within minutes, which is why the hydroxyapatite-binding AMP module exists at all; the computational peptide screen was conducted on their explicit recommendation. A third: on discovering that bovine pancreatic DNase I is already commercially available at roughly 80-160 yuan per 100 mg and widely used, they strategically stopped trying to recombinantly express it and concentrated the synthetic biology effort on the glycoside hydrolases where the EPS matrix offered a real opportunity. Dr. Lei also set a boundary the team kept: any active ingredient in a daily product must be safe and must not disrupt the normal oral microbiome or damage soft tissues.
good.realWorld: The most commercially literate section of the five teams, and notable for restraint. The problem is scoped deliberately narrowly: the project does not aim to replace professional scaling, but to serve adults who cannot or will not undergo frequent scaling with a daily, safe, evidence-based product that interferes with plaque maturation and reduces mineralisation risk before it happens — daily prevention and risk reduction, not treatment of existing calculus or periodontal disease. Target segment is urban young people aged 20-30, students and people one to five years into their first jobs, chosen because they have purchasing power, care about social image and have not yet entrenched habits. Channels are specified rather than gestured at: online seeding on Douyin, Xiaohongshu and Bilibili, e-commerce subscriptions, and offline placement in convenience stores, beauty collection stores and supermarkets, with trial experience areas in beauty collection stores. A B-end clinic seed-trial path runs in parallel with the C-end consumer path, and contingencies are written down (if clinic repeat-purchase is below expectation, optimise usage instructions and physician script training; if C-end subscription retention declines, control ad spend pace and iterate the product experience). Six quarterly milestones run from improving the dual recombinant enzyme lab data and stability, patent drafting and seed trials in three to five clinics, through pilot scale-up and third-party safety testing, to daily chemical regulatory filing, first commercial production, retail rollout and a monthly subscription. A three-year P&L is projected (revenue 45 with net -30 and about 35% gross margin, then revenue 280 with net +120 and about 58% gross margin, then revenue 950 with net +530 and about 65% gross margin). IP strategy notes that existing Chinese patents in this space are mostly single-enzyme or simple multi-enzyme combinations and rarely apply microcapsule encapsulation systematically to oral enzyme care, and acquisition by listed biotech oral care entrants such as Bloomage Biotech or Weimeizi (Saky) is named as the exit after commercial validation. Most creditable: all marketing materials and product claims will state explicitly that the product does not replace professional scaling or periodontal treatment, and the portable chewing gum format is to be marketed only for post-meal freshness with no preventive or anti-calculus claim at all — a team voluntarily giving up its best marketing line because it has not earned it yet. Sustainability is argued concretely rather than with SDG slogans: all four actives are proteins expected to degrade to amino acids and peptides after use, and no live organisms are released.

gemsTakeaway: Their best transferable move is reporting the computational prediction that lost: FoldX picked Y166Q, the bench picked Q172P, and the wiki revises its own ranking and demotes the failed candidate to a mechanistic probe while showing that BCA normalisation rules out protein load as the explanation. A high-school dry lab earns more credibility from one honestly scored wrong prediction with the confound controlled than from three unvalidated ones. Also copy the cheap inspectability trick — export the docked structure as a glTF so a reader can rotate it — and the commercial restraint of marketing a format with no efficacy claim until the evidence exists.
